title: The museum and its props
summary: Not everything in R.E.P.O. is a weapon or a valuable: the game defines props of its own, including a museum piece, and gives cosmetic objects a condition of their own.
body: The game defines props as objects in the world rather than as scenery, which is why something like a museum piece is its own thing.
Cosmetic objects carry a condition of their own, so decoration is not purely visual in the data even if it looks that way in play.
Inside the between-run shop there is a machine for cosmetics, which is where these objects come from rather than from the level.
What this entry does not tell you: prices, what any prop is worth or whether a prop can be damaged. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The game defines its own museum props rather than only scenery.
Cosmetic objects have a condition tracked in the game.
Cosmetics come from a machine in the between-run shop.
The build names the museum's own floors in wood and in concrete, including a floor piece made for hiding.
facts.evidence: asset names: Floor Museum Wood, Floor Museum Concrete Bright NEW, Floor_1x0.5 museum hidey

facts.claim: A broken statue and a broken artwork are named among the museum's props.
facts.evidence: asset names: Broken statue, Broken Artwork Broken Statue

facts.claim: The museum has ambience of its own, kept as separate loops including one for its elevator shaft.
facts.evidence: asset names: Ambience Loop Museum Elevator Shaft, Ambience Loop Museum Maint, Ambience Loop Museum Hell

facts.claim: Its artwork is hung rather than built in: the museum ships painting stands and dirty paintings of its own.
facts.evidence: asset names: Museum Painting Stand, DirtyPainting

facts.claim: The painting stands come in more than one build.
facts.evidence: asset names: Museum Painting Stand H, Museum Painting Stand sss

facts.claim: The paintings have a back of their own, with a colour sheet kept for it.
facts.evidence: asset names: Museum Painting Back, Museum Painting_Back_Albedo

facts.claim: The paintings have a back, a vertical frame and stands with their own sheets.
facts.evidence: asset names: Museum Painting_Back_Albedo, Painting Frame Vertical_Normal, Painting stands_DefaultMaterial_Normal

facts.claim: The museum also ships shadow decals of its own, a round one and a square one.
facts.evidence: asset names: Museum Decal Shadow Round, Museum Decal Shadow Square

facts.claim: The museum ships decals of its own: paper, dirt and hanging dust.
facts.evidence: asset names: Museum Decal Paper01, Museum Decal Dirt01, Museum Decal Hanging Dust Alpha01

facts.claim: The decals are numbered in sets, with dirt two and three and paper two among them.
facts.evidence: asset names: Museum Decal Dirt02, Museum Decal Dirt03, Museum Decal Paper02

facts.claim: The paper and dirt decals run to at least five each.
facts.evidence: asset names: Museum Decal Paper05, Museum Decal Dirt05

facts.claim: The paintings are a set of their own, with a wide landscape, a portrait and a surrealist canvas among them.
facts.evidence: asset names: Painting_H_Landscape, Painting_V_Furman, Painting_V_surrealistic, Painting_S_Tree

facts.claim: The set runs to a signed portrait and a grinning canvas as well.
The decals are numbered further than five: the dirt set reaches seven and the paper set six.
facts.evidence: asset names: Museum Decal Dirt06, Museum Decal Dirt07, Museum Decal Paper06
